uncertainObservations: The disc count is the weakest observation: the front-row discs overlap at their rims and the leftmost sits at the edge of the lit area. Recorded as 7 but treat as low confidence — 6 or 8 are both possible.
Whether the figure is seated or kneeling/standing and leaning cannot be determined; the bench hides her lower body.
The moon's phase is recorded as full/near-full but cloud softens one limb, so a gibbous phase cannot be ruled out.
The number of tool shafts in the pail is not resolvable.

uncertainObservations: Disc count is NOT reliable and I record it as null. Along the front/lower ledge I can individually resolve five flat discs in a left-to-right row. Set slightly higher and behind them I can resolve the upright disc under the chisel, and one further disc near the pail at the right. That gives at least six clearly separable, plausibly seven or eight — but the discs on the upper level partly overlap each other and the bench edge, and at least one may be a plate or a tool tray rather than another disc.
The number of thin tools in the metal pail cannot be counted; roughly four or five rods, heavily overlapping.
Whether the object in her raised hand is a hammer, a mallet or a punch cannot be fully determined, though it reads as a small hammer with a dark head.
The moon's exact phase is obscured by cloud.
The distant skyline cannot be counted into discrete buildings.
